BACKPORT: Revert "r8152: napi hangup fix after disconnect" This reverts commit 0ee1f4734967af8321ecebaf9c74221ace34f2d5. The commit 0ee1f4734967 ("r8152: napi hangup fix after disconnect") adds a check about RTL8152_UNPLUG to determine if calling napi_disable() is invalid in rtl8152_close(), when rtl8152_disconnect() is called. This avoids to use napi_disable() after calling netif_napi_del(). Howver, commit ffa9fec30ca0 ("r8152: set RTL8152_UNPLUG only for real disconnection") causes that RTL8152_UNPLUG is not always set when calling rtl8152_disconnect(). Therefore, I have to revert commit 0ee1f4734967 ("r8152: napi hangup fix after disconnect"), first. And submit another patch to fix it. power_status: Improve battery_charging() If either linepower or the battery thinks were charging, then we probably are. Some devices don't give the status field of linepower, but they do give the status field of the battery. My Sarien for instance does not have linepower.status, and this was the impetus for this CL, because the old ac_charging() function did not work on Sarien (it said not charging, when in fact it was charging). If this breaks any tests by changing the behavior, then those tests are flawed: They thought that the DUT was not charging, when it really was. While were at it, rename ac_charging() to battery_charging(), because that's what really is happening, and simplify the |= logic. power_BatteryDrain: Add client utility test This test drains the battery quickly, as a utility for other tests. It turns the screen and keyboard backlight up as high as possible, and then opens Chrome to a WebGL heavy webpage. It requires that AC power is not supplied, so you will have to turn it off via servo in a server test. You can specify a battery threshold to drain to, and a timeout in seconds. On my Sarien device this puts the battery drain rate at about 35 watts, as compared to about 6 when sitting idle at the login screen with a medium backlight. In conjunction with a USB power load tester (https://amzn.com/B01LKT0OTQ) that draws an additional 10 watts, the DUT drains at about 1% a minute. For the policy_DevicePowerPeakShift and policy_DeviceAdvancedBatteryChargeMode tests that I am writing, which require the DUT to be at about 95% battery (so they can charge), this only takes about 5 minutes. BUG=b:139201701, b:138940522, b:143173004 TEST=test_that -b sarien \ --args='drain_to_percent=90 drain_timeout=300' $DUT power_BatteryDrain Change-Id: Id7373d7b929cfdf3d71ffde37ef3d5dea501bfc7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1867569 Tested-by: Nick Crews (Nov 1 last day) <ncrews@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Derek Beckett <dbeckett@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth: Enable filter duplicated adv offload. This change will reduce by an order of magnitude the number of advertisements the system will need to process when an LE device that distributed an IRK is paired but isn't connected. This isn't a complete solution since the filter duplicate is a best effort solution at best from the controller, so in very noisy environements, it is possible that the controller will be unable to filter duplicates and will send them all up to the host.
